events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.
I'll check what's already in the workspace first, then build the app to fit it.

events.content: All 11 tests pass. Next I'll run the real server, add a book, stop the server, start it again and check the book is still there.

args.command:
cd /workspace && export PORT=3456 DATA_FILE=/tmp/smoke/books.json && rm -rf /tmp/smoke
node server.js & PID=$!; sleep 0.7
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'add: %{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n' -d 'title=The Hobbit&author=J.R.R. Tolkien&notes=Bilbo leaves home.' localhost:3456/books
ID=$(node -e 'console.log(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("/tmp/smoke/books.json","utf8"))[0].id)')
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'finish: %{http_code}\n' -d 'back=home' localhost:3456/books/$ID/finish
kill $PID; wait $PID 2>/dev/null
node server.js & PID=$!; sleep 0.7
echo '--- after restart, home page:'; curl -s localhost:3456/ | grep -A3 'The Hobbit' | head -4
echo '--- book page:'; curl -s localhost:3456/books/$ID | grep -E '<h1>|class="author"|class="notes"|class="meta"|class="share"'
kill $PID; echo '--- file:'; cat /tmp/smoke/books.json

events.content:
The books app is built and works. I ran it end to end: I added a book, marked it finished, restarted the server, and the book was still there with its notes on its own page.

To start it, run `npm start` and open http://localhost:3000.

- **Home page:** shows "Currently reading" (each book has a "Mark finished" button) and "Finished" (with the date you finished it). The "Add a book" form is at the bottom. Title is required; author and notes are optional.
- **Book page:** click a title to see its title, author, reading status and notes. The page shows its own link in a box, so you can copy it and send it to someone.
- **Saving:** books go in `data/books.json`. If that file isn't valid JSON, the app won't start, so it can't overwrite your books. `data/` is in `.gitignore`.
- **Settings:** `PORT`, `DATA_FILE` and `HOST` can be set to change the port, the file location and the address it listens on.

**What I checked:** `npm test` passes all 11 tests (exit code 0). They cover saving and reloading, adding 20 books at once without losing any, the forms and redirects, the book page, a missing title, not-found pages, and making sure anything typed into a form can't inject HTML into the page. I only checked the pages with curl, not in a browser.

Things you should know:
- **Links only work for people who can reach your computer.** A `localhost` link only works on your machine. On your home network, the other person needs your computer's IP address, e.g. `http://192.168.1.20:3000/books/<id>`. For anyone further away, the app would need to be hosted somewhere.
- **Anyone who has the address can make changes, not just view.** With no accounts, they can also add books, mark them finished or edit notes. Book links use random IDs, so people can't guess other books' links, but nothing is really private. If you set `HOST=127.0.0.1`, only your own computer can reach the app, and sharing won't work.
- **I added one thing you didn't ask for:** an "Edit notes" section on each book page, so you can add notes as you go and not only when you first add a book.
- **There's no delete, and no way to move a finished book back to "Currently reading".** For now you'd fix those by editing the JSON file while the app is stopped.

Files: `server.js`, `src/store.js` (saving to the file), `src/app.js` (pages and forms), `test/books.test.js`. I also added `start` and `test` scripts to `package.json`.
